text:
mika: Quick idea — can we prototype an "audit inbox" in the console? a focused place that surfaces "who changed what" with single-click export/ack/escalate actions. think of it like an inbox for compliance events, not raw logs.

samir: love it. high-level: what fields are must-haves for the UI vs export?

mika: must-haves for UI: actor display, actor type (user/service), timestamp, resource touched, brief diff snippet (one-liner), reason/annotation if present, severity tag (config change, policy, quota). exports should contain full context incl. request_id, client_ip, raw diff.

elaine: +1. also need clear PII redaction options per org. some customers want full IPs, others want masked. can we wire through existing export API flags?

kai: we'd need an API shape for the inbox. proposal (very rough):
```json
{
  "event_id": "string",
  "actor_id": "string",
  "actor_display": "string",
  "actor_type": "user|service|integration",
  "resource": "string",
  "action": "string",
  "timestamp": "iso8601",
  "summary_diff": "string",
  "links": { "export": "url", "raw": "url" },
  "severity": "info|warn|critical",
  "org_id": "string",
  "annotations": ["string"]
}
```

zara: would prefer annotations be a string of objects so we can store author + ts + note, but we can start with simple list of strings. important: event ordering & stable cursor for infinite scroll.

jordan: how do we handle retention/quota for exports? exports can be huge. customer tried to export 6mo of audit events yesterday and it blew past their quota. we need rate limits and a async export job model.

mika: agreed. UX idea: quick-export (last 7 days, UI-limited) vs full-export (async NDJSON job with pagination + job-id). quick-export respects org export quota. full-export costs consume export-limits and require approval for >XGB.

samir: telemetry: tag each inbox action (ack, escalate, export, annotate) with rollout_id and routing_policy. we should be able to correlate an escalation to a deployment rollout.

ops-bot: deploy-bot posted: CI-deploy v2.3.1 -> canary started in us-west.

elaine: UX/rollout question — do we surface inbox to everyone or gate to roles? compliance teams want read-only access, infra wants triage rights. need RBAC surface.

kai: backend: store near-realtime stream + snapshot index for UI queries. index by org_id, resource, actor, severity. for export we reuse changefeed exporter. we need to debate schema: should we include full_before/after blobs in the inbox payload? that might bloat the UI.

zara: don't include full blobs in UI. include short diff and offer a "view full" modal which fetches on click (and logs the access event). that helps privacy.

samir: routing policy question: if a customer uses multi-region dedicated, should the inbox aggregate events from all regions in the control plane? or show region-scoped inboxes?

mika: prefer unified inbox with region tag on events and filter controls, but allow region-scoped view for local ops. unified = easier for compliance.

jordan: actionability: add a small set of quick actions: ack, pin, escalate (creates a support/incident), annotate. escalate should POST to our incident API with links.

elaine: from a compliance standpoint, actions must be auditable — action_user, action_time, action_reason. actions should themselves be events that are exportable.

kai: how about rollout plan? canary in console for 10% orgs, feature flag gated. start with read-only inbox + exports, then add actions in phase 2 after RBAC and audit of actions.

mika: timeline suggestion: prototype UI + backend index -> internal alpha (platform + sec) -> public canary with org opt-in -> GA.

samir: API debate: do we expose "inbox" as a dedicated endpoint `/v1/audit/inbox` or as a filtered `/v1/audit/events?inbox_view=true` param? former is cleaner for product semantics.

zara: +1 for dedicated endpoint. easier to evolve separate pagination/cursors and job semantics.

mika: ok next steps: kai to sketch minimal schema + API contract, zara to mock UI flows, samir to list telemetry hooks and quota rules, elaine to draft PII/retention policy options. can everyone drop a quick ack if they can take the item?

kai: I'll take schema + contract.

zara: I'll take mocks.

samir: telemetry + quotas, on it.

elaine: PII/retention draft.

mika: thanks — I'll put a short RFC into the eng-platform backlog and link these items. tagging @security for visibility. :eyes:

ops-bot: security-alert: new RFC created: RFC-2023-audit-inbox by mika.

jordan: small nit — include a "reason required" toggle for orgs that want mandatory change reasons. saves follow-ups later.

mika: good call. I'll add that as an org setting in the docs.

samir: one more: metric idea — "avg time to ack" per org + trendline, to detect neglected changes.

zara: nice. that can feed into Optimize recommendations later.

mika: cool. wrapping up — I'll create the RFC and assign initial owners. we'll reconvene after mocks + schema. :thumbsup:
